start_here: Say to your AI: "Find every other place the file /Volumes/Card/DCIM/clip.mov is, on my other drives and in my own files." It runs tool:media-file-places with that path and your files handed in, and tells you each drive path and file name that holds the same bytes.
no_lists_because: It reads the person's connected drives and the files it is handed in stored.files, and keeps nothing.
instructions: 1. Connect the drive that holds the file and note the file's full path, for example /Volumes/Card/DCIM/clip.mov (it must be on a connected drive, not on the computer's own disk).

2. Say "Find every other place /Volumes/Card/DCIM/clip.mov is." Your AI reads the names and identities of your own files from where you keep them and runs tool:media-file-places through tools:run with {"path": "/Volumes/Card/DCIM/clip.mov", "stored": {"files": {"<name>": {"identity": "1f:..."}}}}; it runs on your computer and takes about 20 seconds.

3. Read the answer: places lists each drive copy (kind drive, with its path, mount and drive name) and, when your own files hold the same bytes, one own-files place with the names they are kept under.

4. Check complete. When it is false, unreadable names the folders that could not be read, so a copy may sit there: fix their access and run it again; files_not_given means none of your own files were handed in, so none of them was checked. A 403 means the file is not on a connected drive; a 400 means you gave a folder.

worked_examples.given: Read from tools/work-on-connected-drives/read-data/file-places.mjs and its test test/file-places.test.mjs (its case with two drives and a Trillion name). I could not run it here: it needs a Mac with drives mounted under /Volumes. Synthetic setup: drives Card and Backup are connected; Card holds DCIM/clip.mov (1048576 bytes); Backup holds Footage/renamed.mov with the same bytes; a different file Backup/Footage/other.mov has the same size but other bytes; the Trillion space holds the identity under /Projects/clip.mov. The identity shown is a made-up 1f: plus 64 hex characters.
worked_examples.hands_back: The answer's result is {"path":"/Volumes/Card/DCIM/clip.mov","identity":"1f:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","byte_length":1048576,"places":[{"kind":"drive","path":"/Volumes/Backup/Footage/renamed.mov","mount":"/Volumes/Backup","drive":"Backup"},{"kind":"drive","path":"/Volumes/Card/DCIM/clip.mov","mount":"/Volumes/Card","drive":"Card"},{"kind":"own-files","identity":"1f:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","names":["/Projects/clip.mov"]}],"complete":true}. The drive places are sorted by path, other.mov is left out because its bytes differ, and the own-files place comes last.
